title: Protocol for Purification of Human ZGRF1 and Its Regulatory Function on RAD51-Mediated D-Loop Formation
protocol: Generate the recombinant bacmid DNA.
Transform DH10Bac competent E. coli cells using 10–25 ng of ZGRF1-(His)6-pDEST20 expression vector.
Add 1 mL SOC medium to the transformed cells.
Shake the cells at 37°C and 200 rpm for 4 hours.
Dilute the cell suspension fivefold and twenty-fivefold with SOC medium.
Plate 100 μL of each dilution on an LB agar plate containing 50 μg/mL kanamycin, 7 μg/mL gentamicin, 10 μg/mL tetracycline, 100 μg/mL Bluo-gal, and 40 μg/mL IPTG.
Incubate the plates at 37°C for 48 hours.
Transfer a white bacterial colony into 3 mL LB culture containing 50 μg/mL kanamycin, 7 μg/mL gentamicin, and 10 μg/mL tetracycline.
Incubate the culture in a shaking incubator at 37°C for 12–16 hours.
Resuspend, lyse, and neutralize the 3 mL E. coli culture with buffers P1, P2, and 3 M potassium acetate (pH 5.5), respectively.
Precipitate bacmid DNA from the supernatant using isopropanol and centrifuge for 15 minutes at 14,000 × g.
Wash the pellet with 70% ethanol, remove the ethanol, and air dry the pellet for 10 minutes at 22°C–25°C.
Dissolve bacmid DNA in 40 μL of 1× TE Buffer, pH 8.0.
Incubate at 4°C for 12–16 hours.
Gently mix the solution by tapping the tube.
Amplify recombinant bacmid DNA using PCR with Sequencing Primers if necessary.
Transfect Sf9 cells in a 6-well plate with the bacmid DNA using Invitrogen Cellfectin II Reagent according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Set up a negative control well without bacmid DNA.
Incubate transfected cells and control wells at 27°C in a humidified incubator for 8–9 days.
Add 0.5–1 mL of fresh medium on day 4–5 after transfection to prevent drying out.
Monitor cell growth until day 8–9; control Sf9 cells should become saturated, while transfected cells should be larger with lower confluence (∼50%).
Collect the primary virus (P1 viral stock) by centrifugation at 500 × g for 5 minutes to remove cells and debris.
Store P1 viral stock at 4°C for up to 2–3 months.
Grow Sf9 cells to a density of 2 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Transfer 30 mL of cells into a 175 cm² cell culture flask.
Swirl the flask gently and place it in a 27°C humidified incubator for 30 minutes to allow attachment.
Add 1 mL of P1 viral stock into the Sf9 cell culture flask.
Swirl the flask gently to mix.
Incubate the cells for 6-7 days in a 27°C humidified incubator or until about 40%-50% cells appear lysed.
Collect 30 mL of the Sf9 cell culture medium and transfer to sterile 50 mL snap-cap tubes.
Centrifuge the tubes at 500 × g for 5 minutes to remove cells and debris.
Store the P2 viral stock at 4°C for 2-3 months.
Repeat the process to generate the P3 viral stock.
Critical: The P3 viral stock should be made fresh and used for protein expression within 2-3 weeks.
Express recombinant GST-(TEV)-ZGRF1-(His)6 in Hi5 cells.
Infect 5 × 50 mL Hi5 cells (1 × 10^6 cells/mL) with 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5 mL fresh P3 viral stock for an expression test experiment.
Incubate the cells at 27°C at 170 rpm for 40-44 hours.
Harvest the cells and perform an anti-GST western blot to determine an appropriate dilution of P3 viral stock for best expression.
Innoculate 150 mL Hi5 cells into two 1,000 mL Erlenmeyer flasks and incubate at 27°C at 170 rpm.
Maintain the cells for 1 day and expand to 300 mL (0.6 × 10^6 cells/mL) for each flask.
Infect the cells with 10-15 mL fresh P3 viral stock when Hi5 cells are in the mid-logarithmic phase of growth at a density of 1 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Incubate the infected cells at 27°C at 170 rpm for 40-44 hours.
Thaw frozen cells (∼8 g) and resuspend in chilled Protein Lysis Buffer.
Transfer the suspension into a beaker placed on ice.
Stir the mixture gently for 15 min using a magnetic stirrer at 4°C.
Sonicate the mixture at 50 amplitude with a 1/2 inch diameter probe, for 30 s three separate times on ice.
Maintain cell mixture at low temperature near 4°C.
Keep the mixture on ice for at least 1 min after each 30 s sonication.
Clarify the crude lysate at 100,000 × g for 30 min.
Keep a small aliquot of the clarified lysate for further analysis.
Pack 2 mL of Glutathione Sepharose 4B resin into a gravity column.
Wash the resin with 20 mL of ddH2O.
Wash the resin with 20 mL of Binding Buffer.
Split the equilibrated resin into two 50 mL snap-cap tubes.
Mix the clarified cell lysate (∼100 mL) with the affinity resin at 4°C for 1.5 h on a rotary platform at 40 rpm.
Collect the resin in a chromatography column, drain by gravity for about 20 min.
Wash the resin with 50 mL Binding Buffer, three times.
Combine the wash and keep a small aliquot of wash for further analysis.
Wash the resin with 50 mL Binding Buffer plus 1 mM ATP, followed by 50 mL Binding buffer plus 5 mM MgCl2 to remove additional protein contaminants.
Elute GST-(TEV)-ZGRF1-(His)6 with 3 mL Glutathione Elution Buffer at 4°C for 10 min by repeatedly passing the eluate through the packed resin.
Repeat the elution step three additional times with fresh Glutathione Elution Buffer.
Keep a small aliquot of each eluate for further analysis.
Take a small amount of the resin after elution for further analysis.
Pack 0.5 mL of Ni-NTA Agarose resin into a narrow chromatography column.
Wash the resin with 5 mL of ddH2O.
Wash the resin with 5 mL of Binding Buffer.
Transfer the resin to a new 15 mL snap-cap tube.
Mix resin with the eluate (∼12 mL) from the previous affinity purification step at 4°C for 2.5 h on a rotary platform.
Transfer the resin suspension back to the chromatography column and drain by gravity.
Wash the resin with 50 mL Binding Buffer, three times.
Combine the wash and keep a small aliquot of wash for further analysis.
Wash the resin with 25 mL Imidazole Wash Buffer.
Keep a small aliquot for further analysis.
Elute the GST-(TEV)-ZGRF1-(His)6 protein with 0.6 mL Imidazole Elution Buffer at 4°C for 10 min by repeatedly passing the eluate through the packed resin.
Repeat the elution with 0.6 mL fresh Imidazole Elution Buffer.
Keep a small aliquot of each eluate for further analysis.
Take a small amount of the resin for further analysis.
Analyze samples by SDS-PAGE.
Stain gels with Coomassie Brilliant Blue.
Load Marker, All Blue Prestained Protein Standards (Bio-Rad) from left.
Load GST-affinity Wash and Eluate sample from GST resin.
Load GST resin after elution.
Load Ni-NTA Wash and Eluate sample from Ni-NTA resin.
Load 15 mM imidazole wash from Ni-NTA resin.
Load Ni-NTA resin after elution.
Add 44.5 mL Dialysis Buffer to a 50 mL conical tube.
Add 4 mL of Dialysis Buffer into the Slide-A-Lyzer MINI Dialysis Device.
Decant buffer by shaking the device.
Apply combined protein sample (∼1.2 mL) into the dialysis device.
Place the device slowly into the 50 mL conical tube containing the Dialysis Buffer.
Cap the conical tube securely and mix gently on an orbital shaker at 4°C.
Continue dialysis for 2 hours at 4°C.
Change the Dialysis Buffer in the 50 mL conical tube.
Continue dialysis for 12–14 hours at 4°C.
Collect the dialyzed protein sample.
Apply the sample to a Corning Spin-X Ultrafiltration Concentrator (500 μL, 50 kDa cutoff) to further concentrate to ∼500 μL.
Split the purified ZGRF1 protein into 5 μL aliquots.
Freeze the aliquoted samples in liquid nitrogen.
Store the frozen samples at -80°C.
Prepare the pBluescript SK+ plasmid DNA using QIAGEN Plasmid Mini or Midi kit.
Examine the topological state of the plasmid DNA by 0.9% agarose gel electrophoresis.
Critical: The D-loop formation efficiency is sensitive to the topological state of the duplex DNA.
The supercoiled form of plasmid DNA should be the major form, ideally ≥90% of total DNA.
5′-end Radiolabel the 90-mer oligonucleotide.
Purify the 90-mer oligonucleotide from a 10% polyacrylamide gel.
Measure the DNA concentration spectrophotometrically.
Store the purified oligonucleotide at -80°C.
Add reagents in a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube on ice and mix.
Incubate the labeling reaction at 37°C for 1 h.
Inactivate T4 polynucleotide kinase by incubating at 65°C for 20 min.
Remove unincorporated [γ-32P]-ATP using Micro Bio-Spin P-6 Gel Columns according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Measure the DNA concentration spectrophotometrically.
Store the labeled oligonucleotide at -20°C (shielded).
Incubate 0-0.5 μg ZGRF1 with 10 nM 32P-labeled 90-mer oligonucleotide or dsDNA at 30°C for 1 hour in reaction buffer containing 20 mM Tris-Cl, pH 7.5, 10 mM MgCl2, 50 mM KCl and 1 mM DTT.
Treat reactions with SDS (0.1%) and proteinase K (0.5 mg/mL) for 10 minutes at 30°C to deproteinize.
Resolve the treated reactions in a 15% polyacrylamide gel in TBE buffer.
Assemble reaction mixtures in 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes on ice.
Add 9.4 μL master mix to each tube for D-loop formation assay.
Incubate the mixture at 37°C for 10 minutes to allow RAD51 to engage ssDNA.
Add 0.6 μL human RAD51 protein (4.5 μM) to a final concentration of 216 nM.
Incubate the reactions at 25°C for 2 minutes after adding RAD54.
Add 0.5 μL human RAD54 protein (2.25 μM) to a final concentration of 90 nM.
Add 1.0 μL human ZGRF1 protein to a final concentration of 40 nM.
Use 1.0 μL Dialysis Buffer as negative control.
Immediately add 1.0 μL pBluescript SK+ plasmid DNA to a final concentration of 48 μM base pairs and mix.
Incubate at 30°C for 5, 10, and 20 min.
Add 12.5 μL of 1% SDS and 2 μL of proteinase K (10 mg/mL) to stop the reaction.
Incubate at 37°C for 5 min to deproteinize the reaction.
Withdraw 8 μL of the above deproteinized reaction mixture, and add 2 μL of agarose gel loading buffer.
Resolve the mixture in a 0.9% agarose gel in TBE buffer at 130 mA for 90 min at 25°C.
Dry the gel onto Whatman 3MM chromatography paper in a gel dryer for 1 h at 80°C.
Subject the dried gel to phosphorimaging analysis.
Prepare a master mix of D-loop reaction buffer on ice in a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Add 20 μL yeast Rad51 protein (10 μM) to achieve a final concentration of 0.8 μM.
Incubate the reaction for 10 min at 37°C.
Add 20 μL yeast RPA protein (2.5 μM) to reach a final concentration of 200 nM.
Incubate the reaction for 5 min at 30°C.
Add 20 μL yeast Rad54 protein (3 μM) to achieve a final concentration of 240 nM.
Incubate the reaction for 2 min at 23°C.
Add 20 μL negatively supercoiled pBluescript SK+ plasmid DNA (600 μM base pairs) to reach a final concentration of 48 μM base pairs and mix thoroughly.
Incubate at 30°C for 4 min.
Extract yeast Rad51-made D-loops using phenol-chloroform.
Add 4.5 μL of 10% SDS to the reaction mixture.
Add 10 μL of proteinase K (10 mg/mL) to the reaction mixture.
Incubate at 37°C for 15 min.
Add 260 μL phenol-chloroform-isoamyl alcohol (25:24:1).
Mix thoroughly by vortexing.
Centrifuge at 22°C–25°C at 17,000 × g for 5 min.
Transfer the upper aqueous phase into a fresh tube.
Add 260 μL chloroform to the transferred phase.
Mix thoroughly by vortexing.
Centrifuge at 22°C–25°C at 17,000 × g for 5 min.
Transfer the upper aqueous phase into another fresh tube without any of the chloroform.
Store this tube at 4°C.
Equilibrate the Zeba Spin-desalting Column with 15 mL Buffer H (35 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5, 1 mM DTT, 9.3 mM MgCl2, and 30 mM KCl).
Apply the aqueous phase solution to the column without disturbing the surface.
Collect the flow-through in 200 μL portions into fresh tubes.
Elute the column with Buffer H.
Collect the eluate in 15 portions of 200 μL each.
Determine the D-loop content in each fraction by gel electrophoresis in a 0.9% agarose gel in TBE buffer.
Perform phosphorimaging analysis.
Combine eluates containing the bulk of D-loops for purification.
Determine concentration of purified D-loops by side-by-side comparison with a known amount of 32P-labeled 90-mer oligonucleotide.
Prepare 8 μL of D-loop dissociation buffer per reaction, containing 25 mM Tris-Cl (pH 7.5), 1 mM DTT, 2 mM ATP, and 2 mM MgCl2 in a microcentrifuge tube.
Add 1 μL of ZGRF1 protein (2.5–20 nM) to each reaction and incubate on ice for 10 min.
Add 1 μL of purified D-loops (22 nM) to each reaction and mix thoroughly.
Incubate D-loops (∼2.2 nM) with ZGRF1 (2.5–20 nM) at 37°C for 10 min.
Add 0.5 μL of 10% SDS and 1 μL of proteinase K (10 mg/mL) to the reaction mixture.
Incubate at 37°C for 5 min.
Add 3 μL of agarose gel loading buffer.
Resolve reaction mixtures in a 0.9% agarose gel in TBE buffer at 130 mA for 90 min at 25°C.
Dry the gel onto Whatman 3MM chromatography paper in a gel dryer for 1 h at 80°C.
Subject the dried gel to phosphorimaging analysis.
